company_claims.text: Halvane builds store operations software that store associates use for inventory and shelf replenishment in mid-size grocery chains.
In June 2026 Halvane announced a pilot of ShelfSight, camera-based out-of-stock detection, with two grocery chains.
Halvane committed to WCAG 2.2 AA for its associate mobile app and runs automated accessibility checks in CI on every pull request.
The Store Platform role requires Python or JavaScript, REST APIs, Git and automated testing; computer vision and web accessibility are preferred.
The Store Platform team may be preparing to extend ShelfSight beyond the pilot.
Halvane employs about 420 people in Chicago and Toronto; engineering is organised in product teams: Store Platform, Associate App and ShelfSight.

company_profile.note: "mid-size grocery chains" (C1) are customers; Halvane's own size comes from C6

letter.subject: Application: Junior Software Engineer, Store Platform

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role on the Store Platform team at Halvane Retail Systems. Two things Halvane has published match work I have already started: the ShelfSight pilot announced in June 2026 and the commitment to WCAG 2.2 AA for the associate app. The posting also lists computer vision and web accessibility as preferred skills.

Accessibility is where my evidence is strongest. I built AltCheck, a GitHub Action that flags images without alt text in HTML pull requests, and three student club websites adopted it. Your engineering blog describes automated accessibility checks running in CI on every pull request, which is the workflow AltCheck was built for: a check that runs where developers already review code.

ShelfScan, my computer vision course project, is a prototype rather than a product. I built OpenCV preprocessing and trained a PyTorch model that counts products on shelf photos, using a public dataset; its accuracy was not formally measured. It taught me how much work separates a classroom model from a store pilot, which is why ShelfSight interests me.

For everyday platform work, RouteWise is my most complete project: a FastAPI service with REST endpoints over PostgreSQL, built with two classmates, covered by pytest tests, and used by four volunteer coordinators during a three-week pilot.

If the Store Platform team is preparing to extend ShelfSight beyond the pilot, I would be glad to contribute tested services and accessible web features around it. I would welcome a conversation about where the team needs help first.
